title: Prefer native interactive elements over ARIA substitutes
statement: Buttons, links, checkboxes, and form controls are built from the elements the language provides, and ARIA roles are added only where no native element expresses the pattern.
rationale: A native element arrives with its role, its keyboard behaviour, and its state reporting already correct, whereas a role attached to a generic element supplies only the name and leaves every behaviour to be reimplemented.
implementation: Replace clickable generic elements with the button or anchor the interaction actually is, choosing the anchor when it navigates and the button when it acts. Where a role must remain, implement the keyboard behaviour and state the role's specification requires.

verification.method: Enumerate interactive elements in the served response and report those whose role is supplied by an attribute on a generic element.

caution: The justification for this record is conformance with the cited criterion. No search surface is documented to measure it, and none is claimed to.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value

title: Make every interactive control reachable by keyboard
statement: Every action the interface offers can be reached and performed using the keyboard alone, and focus can leave any component it can enter.
rationale: A control reachable only by pointer is unavailable to anyone navigating by keyboard, and a component that traps focus makes the rest of the page unreachable for the remainder of the visit.
implementation: Walk each journey with the keyboard alone and fix what cannot be reached, usually by using a focusable element rather than adding a tab index to a generic one. In a dialog, confine focus deliberately and return it to the trigger on close.

verification.method: Traverse each critical journey using only keyboard input and record every control that could not be reached, activated, or escaped.

caution: Automated scanning finds only part of this. A keyboard traversal by a person remains necessary, so this record is not fully verifiable by tooling.

title: Keep the focused element visible and unobscured
statement: The element holding focus has a visible indicator, and no sticky header, floating bar, cookie notice, or overlay hides it when focus moves through the page.
rationale: Without a visible indicator a keyboard reader cannot tell where they are, and an indicator scrolled beneath a fixed element is present but invisible, which fails for the same reason.
implementation: Keep the default indicator or replace it with one of at least equal visibility, and add scroll padding equal to the height of any fixed element so focus never lands underneath it.

verification.method: Tab through each page and capture the viewport at every stop, confirming the indicator is both drawn and unobstructed.

caution: Two separate criteria apply here, one for the indicator existing and one for it not being covered. Both are cited, and neither is a search requirement.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)

title: Associate every form control with a persistent label
statement: Each input, select, and text area has a programmatically associated label that remains visible while the field is being filled, rather than a placeholder that disappears on entry.
rationale: A placeholder used as a label vanishes exactly when the reader needs to check what they are typing, and it is not reliably announced, so the field's purpose is lost to both groups at once.
implementation: Add a label element referencing the control, or wrap the control in one, and keep the placeholder for an example value only. Do not substitute a title attribute or an adjacent unassociated caption.

verification.method: Compute the accessible name of every form control in the served response and report controls whose name is empty or comes only from a placeholder.

caution: The cited criterion requires labels or instructions. Requiring the label to remain visible during entry goes slightly beyond its text and is included because the failure it prevents is common and observable.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions

title: Meet the contrast minimum for text and interface components
statement: Body and heading text meets the published contrast ratio against its background at its rendered size, and the visual boundaries of interactive components meet the ratio published for non-text content.
rationale: Contrast below the published ratio makes text unreadable for a large group of readers under ordinary conditions such as glare or an ageing display, and the ratio is measurable rather than a matter of taste.
implementation: Compute the ratio for each text and background pair in the design tokens, correct the token rather than the individual component, and check the states as well as the resting appearance. Text over an image needs a scrim or a solid backing.

verification.method: Sample computed foreground and background colours from the rendered page and report pairs below the published ratio for their text size.

caution: Automated sampling cannot evaluate text drawn over photographs or gradients, so those cases stay unresolved by tooling and need review by a person.

title: Provide a skip link past repeated navigation
statement: Each page offers a mechanism, reachable as the first focusable item, that moves focus past the header and navigation directly to the main content region.
rationale: Without it a keyboard reader traverses every navigation item on every page before reaching the content, which makes the repeated block a cost paid once per page rather than once per site.
implementation: Place the link first in the document, target the main landmark by identifier, and reveal it on focus rather than hiding it in a way that removes it from the focus order. Confirm focus actually lands in the target region and not merely that the address changed.

verification.method: Focus the first item on each page, activate it, and record where focus lands relative to the main landmark.

caution: A skip link is one of several mechanisms the cited criterion accepts. A correct landmark structure can satisfy it instead, so the presence of the link is not the only passing outcome.
